clue.text: Chorals composed by a student

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the clue word are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone writes choral pieces as a student exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, or a pupil holding an award, is a classic synonym for a learner.

clue.text: Spanish agreements covering the French over a Central European area

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier pieces sit above the next one
covering means the Spanish yeses wrap round the French article

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes, so two agreements give it twice
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Spanish treaties that include France govern a region of central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts LE inside SISI, giving SILESI, and 'over' sets that above A in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic region now mostly in Poland, partly in the Czech Republic and Germany.

clue.text: Memorial erected when death's shattered a person

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word death with its S, the 's read as 'has' in the surface
a person means one

explanation.surface: A gravestone is put up after a death has devastated someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' acts on DEATHS plus ONE; 'erected when' just links, with the memorial pictured being put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone set over a grave records the dead person, a kind of monument.

clue.text: The beast overturned everything to some degree

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down light the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: everything means all
an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree

explanation.surface: An animal tipped over everything a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' makes LLA; 'to' only links it to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American pack animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Determined views of a judge cut short and edited

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word for a judge is lopped off

parts.note: a referee judges a match

indicators.note: edited means revised, so the letters of the word and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge's opinions, abridged and revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' leaves REFERE; 'edited' turns AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Public votes on a single question settle what the people think: views decided by ballot.

clue.text: Unexpectedly fail to approve

explanation.surface: Something breaks down without warning before it can be sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text's '15' is the count (5,2) misread; there is no cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down suddenly under strain is one sense; to praise or talk up something highly is the other.

clue.text: A Greek island without road lines

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the island goes round the road

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A Greek island has no railway or road links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, so COS wraps RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes or strings are lengths of thin line.

clue.text: Wanting the biggest share in the end?

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
most means the greatest part

explanation.surface: Someone greedy for the lion's share, at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the word means hindmost, nearest the back or stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost or furthest to the rear, so placed at the final point.

clue.text: Jack's a scoundrel!

explanation.surface: Jack is denounced as a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in a pack of cards is also called this, and the word also means a dishonest rascal.

clue.text: Excuse for writing a foreword perhaps

explanation.surface: A foreword serves as a cover story for the writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: a foreword is writing that comes before the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason given to hide the real one; read in two parts, words placed ahead of the main body of a book.

clue.text: Politician owns a place abroad

parts.note: L stands for a Liberal
owns means has

explanation.surface: A politician has a property overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tibet, a city far from Britain.

clue.text: Eve is a naval officer

explanation.surface: A woman named Eve serves as an officer at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve was Adam's partner, the earliest wife, hence the pun on the merchant ship's deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was the earliest companion in Genesis; the rank is the officer next below the captain on a merchant ship.

clue.text: Aromatic stuff produced in America getting as far as the ship maybe

indicators.note: getting is read as getting rearranged, signalling that the letters are shuffled

parts.note: SS is steamship, an example of a ship

explanation.surface: A fragrant American product travels all the way to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a weak anagram signal working on ASFARAS plus SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American tree whose bark and roots give a fragrant oil and flavouring.

clue.text: The magistrate concerned with 10

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the clue to 10 across begins with Eve, so the reference supplies her name

explanation.surface: A magistrate deals with case number ten.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was an old English local official, such as a shire magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon England the chief local officer of a shire or town acted as a judge.

clue.text: Bouquet given in an extra romantic way

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the run extra romantic

explanation.surface: Flowers presented in an especially loving manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell.

clue.text: There are people in all the houses here

definitions.text: There are people in all the houses here

parts.words: There are people in all the houses here
parts.note: houses suggests homes, but a theatre's house is its audience, and full houses fill these halls

explanation.surface: Every house in this street is occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Halls where audiences sit, so each holds a theatre house.

clue.text: Woodland home with directions for its occupation

indicators.note: the home is occupied by the directions, so they go inside it

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
west and fore (towards the front of a ship) are both directions

explanation.surface: A forest house comes with instructions for its tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for its occupation' puts W and FORE inside NEST, after its NE; 'with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient royal hunting ground in Hampshire, southern England, now a national park.

clue.text: Men struggling to earn a living

definitions.text: Men struggling to earn a living

parts.words: Men struggling to earn a living
parts.note: seems to mean men hard up, but these men grapple with opponents for pay

explanation.surface: Men having a hard time making ends meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional grapplers earn their pay by fighting on the mat.

clue.text: One values it — most are badly-made

indicators.note: badly made means put together wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone assessing it says most are shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who judges worth or calculates cost is an appraiser.

clue.text: A bird for the farmworker's packed lunch?

explanation.surface: A bird ends up as a farm labourer's sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it in two: food eaten out in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A large thrush that winters in Britain; read as two words, meals taken in the meadow.

clue.text: Soldiers going into action charge

indicators.note: going into means the soldiers are placed inside the word for action

parts.note: a fight is military action
RE, Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops go into battle and charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an attack but means a fee for carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried, or the fee paid for carrying them.

clue.text: The child a leading journalist bore

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an editor, ED, heads a paper

explanation.surface: An editor's toddler was carried along.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something is to bear it; past tense matches.

clue.text: Artiste who may well give his partner a lift

definitions.text: Artiste who may well give his partner a lift

parts.words: Artiste who may well give his partner a lift
parts.note: sounds like someone offering a ride, but a male ballet dancer lifts the ballerina

explanation.surface: A performer who might drive his partner home.
explanation.definitionFit: A male ballet performer, who raises the ballerina in a pas de deux.

clue.text: Demand and get correct result

explanation.surface: Someone insists and gets the right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' rounds off the surface; the adjective sense is precise.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on and obtain payment is one sense; precise or accurate is the other.

clue.text: A shade of caution

explanation.surface: A colour that warns.
explanation.walkthrough: On British traffic lights the yellow-orange light between red and green warns drivers to prepare to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-orange colour; also the traffic light that signals care.

clue.text: Stockholder who is primarily interested in growth

definitions.text: Stockholder who is primarily interested in growth

parts.words: Stockholder who is primarily interested in growth
parts.note: sounds like an investor seeking capital growth, but the stock is livestock and the growth is fattening the herd

explanation.surface: An investor focused on growth stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher keeps livestock and wants the animals to put on weight.

clue.text: The Arab ruler caught up in wrongdoing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the ruler's title is read from the bottom

parts.note: an emir is an Arab ruler

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler is embroiled in misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EMIR into RIME; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence against the law.

clue.text: The story gripping novices in France

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the story surrounds the novices

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
L is a learner, so two Ls are novices

explanation.surface: A gripping tale about beginners in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a bare 'in France': a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in northern France.

clue.text: Dare begin reforming the Cloth?

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A challenge to start reforming the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Cloth' suggests the clergy, but it is a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm twill fabric used for raincoats.

clue.text: Machine is modern, but gets hot inside

indicators.note: inside means the hot letter goes within the word for modern

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the latest
H is hot on taps

explanation.surface: A new machine overheats internally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool for shaping wood or metal by spinning it, an example of a machine.

clue.text: A suggestion offered about royalty's housing

indicators.note: about means round, so the suggestion surrounds the royal letters

parts.note: a trace is a slight suggestion or hint
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

explanation.surface: A suggestion is made concerning where the royals live.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of joined houses is a form of residential building.

clue.text: He'd drive a bullock with little hesitation

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone would drive cattle without much pause.
explanation.definitionFit: One who guides a vehicle or animal is a driver.
